title: Third Word Worships Spiritual Lightness And Beliefs Security

questions.question: In the comparison, what do the two travelers stand for?
questions.answer: One stands for people who obey Allah’s law, and the other stands for people who rebel and follow their desires.

questions.question: What does the road represent in this passage?
questions.answer: It represents human life, beginning from the world of spirits, going through the grave, and continuing to the hereafter.

questions.question: What do the kit-bag and rifle symbolize?
questions.answer: They symbolize worship and being mindful of Allah.

questions.question: Why does worship seem heavy at first but actually bring ease?
questions.answer: It may look difficult on the outside, but in reality it gives deep inner comfort, strength, and relief.

questions.question: What important belief is declared in the prayer mentioned in the passage?
questions.answer: The worshipper testifies that only Allah is truly worthy of worship.

questions.question: How does this belief change the way a person sees the world?
questions.answer: It helps the person see Allah’s mercy, wisdom, and care in everything.

questions.question: According to the passage, who controls harm and benefit?
questions.answer: Allah alone controls them.

questions.question: Why does the worshipper make du‘a to Allah?
questions.answer: Because he knows Allah is merciful, generous, and the One who can truly help.

questions.question: What does the worshipper do after seeing that everything is under Allah’s command?
questions.answer: He seeks protection in Allah, trusts Him, and depends on Him.

questions.question: What is the result of this trust in Allah?
questions.answer: It gives the believer strength, safety, and firm confidence.

questions.question: According to the passage, what is the source of real bravery?
questions.answer: Real bravery comes from belief in Allah and worship.

questions.question: What is the source of cowardice in the passage?
questions.answer: It comes from going astray and living without true guidance.

questions.question: What example is given to show the courage of a believer?
questions.answer: A believer with a bright heart would not panic even at a huge frightening event, but would look at it with awe at Allah’s power.

questions.question: What example is given to show the fear of a person without true faith?
questions.answer: A person with only outward knowledge but no heart became terrified when he saw a comet and feared disaster.

questions.question: What does the passage say about human power and resources?
questions.answer: It says they are very small and limited.

questions.question: If human ability is so limited, why are worship and trust in Allah such a great blessing?
questions.answer: Because people have huge needs and many fears, so they need Allah’s help, unity, and support.

questions.question: Which two kinds of people are contrasted at the start of the passage?
questions.answer: People who submit to divine guidance and people who rebel by following their own desires.

questions.question: How is the journey of life described?
questions.answer: It is described as a path that starts before this world, passes through death, and continues into the next life.

questions.question: In the comparison, what do the traveler’s supplies and weapon mean?
questions.answer: They mean worship and fear of Allah.

questions.question: What lesson is taught by calling worship an “apparent burden”?
questions.answer: It teaches that worship may seem hard at first, but it actually brings great inner ease.

questions.question: What does the worshipper affirm during prayer?
questions.answer: He affirms that there is no true god except Allah.

questions.question: How does this belief help the worshipper understand creation?
questions.answer: He understands that all provision, creation, harm, and benefit are in Allah’s control.

questions.question: What two qualities of Allah are especially linked to this understanding in the passage?
questions.answer: Allah’s wisdom and His mercy.

questions.question: Why does the worshipper feel able to turn to Allah in du‘a?
questions.answer: Because he believes Allah’s mercy and generosity are wide and always available.

questions.question: How does seeing all things under Allah’s command affect the believer’s attitude?
questions.answer: It makes him seek refuge in Allah and place his trust in Him.

questions.question: What protection does faith give against troubles?
questions.answer: It strengthens the person inwardly and gives steady confidence during hardships.

questions.question: How are virtue and courage connected in the passage?
questions.answer: True goodness is connected to courage through faith and worship.

questions.question: How are sin and cowardice connected in the passage?
questions.answer: Wrongdoing and straying from guidance lead to fearfulness.

questions.question: What contrast is made between an illuminated heart and a mind without heart?
questions.answer: The illuminated heart stays calm before frightening events, while the mind without heart becomes anxious and shaken.

questions.question: Why is the story of the comet included?
questions.answer: It shows that outward learning alone does not give peace if faith is missing.

questions.question: What does the passage say about the size of human needs compared with human ability?
questions.answer: Human needs are countless, while human ability is tiny.

questions.question: What final conclusion is given about worship and reliance on Allah?
questions.answer: They are a great gain, joy, and blessing for weak and needy human beings.

questions.question: What does the passage say the obedient traveler represents?
questions.answer: A person who submits to Allah’s law.

questions.question: What does the rebellious traveler represent?
questions.answer: A person who follows personal desires instead of divine guidance.

questions.question: What stages are included in the road of life as explained here?
questions.answer: It includes the Spirit World, life in this world, the grave, and the hereafter.

questions.question: How are worship and fear of Allah pictured in the comparison?
questions.answer: They are pictured as equipment carried by the traveler.

questions.question: What is the difference between how worship looks and what it really gives?
questions.answer: It may look like a load, but it actually gives peace and relief inside.

questions.question: During prayer, what testimony opens the way to hope and mercy?
questions.answer: The testimony that only Allah is truly worthy of worship.

questions.question: Why does this testimony make the worshipper feel that mercy is near?
questions.answer: Because he sees that the world is in the care of one wise and compassionate Lord.

questions.question: What belief about provision is taught in this part of the passage?
questions.answer: That Allah alone is the true Provider.

questions.question: What belief about events in life is taught by saying harm and benefit are in Allah’s hand?
questions.answer: It means nothing reaches a person outside Allah’s control and wisdom.

questions.question: What actions grow out of this belief in Allah’s control?
questions.answer: A person makes du‘a, seeks refuge in Allah, trusts Him, and relies on Him.

questions.question: What emotional result comes from these actions?
questions.answer: The person becomes stronger, calmer, and more secure.

questions.question: According to the passage, where does true courage come from?
questions.answer: It comes from belief and worship.

questions.question: What does the passage teach about people who are far from guidance?
questions.answer: They become more fearful and weak-hearted.

questions.question: How does the believer respond to a terrifying event in the example given?
questions.answer: He remains calm and sees it as a sign of Allah’s power.

questions.question: How does the faithless philosopher respond to the comet?
questions.answer: He becomes frightened and worried that disaster will happen.

questions.question: What truth about human beings prepares the reader for the final message of the passage?
questions.answer: Human beings are weak, needy, and exposed to many troubles.

questions.question: Based on that human weakness, why are tawhid and trust in Allah so important?
questions.answer: Because they give help, peace, and meaning to a person who cannot manage life alone.

questions.question: Who are the two travelers said to symbolize?
questions.answer: They symbolize the obedient believer and the rebellious person who follows desires.

questions.question: What larger reality does the path in the comparison point to?
questions.answer: It points to the whole journey of human life until the hereafter.

questions.question: Why are worship and fear of Allah compared to travel gear and a weapon?
questions.answer: Because they prepare and protect a person on life’s journey.

questions.question: What does the passage teach about the “weight” of worship?
questions.answer: Its difficulty is only on the surface, while its true meaning brings deep ease.

questions.question: What statement of faith is mentioned from the prayer?
questions.answer: The statement that there is no god but Allah.

questions.question: What does the worshipper discover in everything through this faith?
questions.answer: He discovers signs of Allah’s mercy and care.

questions.question: How does belief in Allah as the only Creator and Provider affect a person’s thinking?
questions.answer: It frees the person from thinking that other things have independent power.

questions.question: Why is Allah’s wisdom important in the argument of this passage?
questions.answer: It shows that events are not pointless or random.

questions.question: Why is Allah’s compassion important in the passage?
questions.answer: It gives the believer hope that Allah’s kindness and mercy are always present.

questions.question: After recognizing these truths, what does the believer do?
questions.answer: He turns to Allah in du‘a, seeks shelter in Him, and trusts Him.

questions.question: How does trust in Allah affect a believer when facing disasters?
questions.answer: It gives inner protection and strong confidence.

questions.question: What relationship does the passage make between faith and bravery?
questions.answer: Faith and worship produce real bravery.

questions.question: What relationship does the passage make between misguidance and fear?
questions.answer: Misguidance produces cowardice.

questions.question: What is the main point of the comparison between the believer and the philosopher?
questions.answer: The believer has calm strength through faith, while the other has anxiety because he lacks spiritual certainty.

questions.question: What does the passage say about the limits of human strength?
questions.answer: Human strength reaches only a small distance and cannot cover all our needs and fears.

questions.question: What reaches farther than human power, according to the passage?
questions.answer: Our hopes, wishes, pains, and worries reach very far.

questions.question: What final message does the passage give about worship and reliance on Allah?
questions.answer: They are a huge benefit and mercy for the human soul because people are weak and needy.

questions.question: At the beginning of the passage, what is the rebellious nafs told to understand?
questions.answer: It is told that the two travelers represent the obedient and the rebellious.

questions.question: What kind of person is represented by the rebellious traveler?
questions.answer: A person who chooses personal desires over Allah’s guidance.

questions.question: How is life’s road described from beginning to end?
questions.answer: It begins from the Spirit World, passes through the grave, and goes on to the hereafter.

questions.question: What do the travel items stand for in the explanation?
questions.answer: They stand for worship and fear of Allah.

questions.question: Why is worship not truly a hardship, even if it seems like one?
questions.answer: Because it gives the soul relief, meaning, and strength beyond what can easily be described.

questions.question: What does the worshipper say in prayer that shapes his whole outlook?
questions.answer: He bears witness that only Allah is truly worthy of worship.

questions.question: How does this statement lead the worshipper to see mercy around him?
questions.answer: It makes him realize that everything is under one merciful Lord.

questions.question: What beliefs about Allah are listed to strengthen the worshipper’s heart?
questions.answer: That Allah alone creates and provides, controls harm and benefit, acts with wisdom, and has abundant mercy.

questions.question: What is the connection between these beliefs and supplication?
questions.answer: These beliefs give the worshipper confidence to ask Allah for help.

questions.question: What does the believer understand about all created things?
questions.answer: He understands that they are under Allah’s command.

questions.question: What three things does the believer then do with his heart?
questions.answer: He seeks refuge in Allah, trusts Him, and relies on Him.

questions.question: What is the spiritual result of doing that?
questions.answer: He becomes protected inwardly and gains full confidence.

questions.question: According to the passage, what gives a person true courage?
questions.answer: Belief in Allah and worship.

questions.question: What makes a person cowardly?
questions.answer: Misguidance and wrongdoing.

questions.question: How does the example of the exploding earth serve the passage’s message?
questions.answer: It shows how strong a believer’s heart can become through faith.

questions.question: What weakness is shown in the story of the frightened philosopher?
questions.answer: A person may have worldly learning but still lack peace and courage without faith.

questions.question: Why does the passage emphasize that human needs are countless?
questions.answer: To show that people desperately need Allah’s help and cannot rely on themselves.

questions.question: What four things are named as great blessings for the human spirit at the end?
questions.answer: Worship, affirming Allah’s oneness, trusting Allah, and submitting to Him.

questions.question: What two groups of people are symbolized by the travelers in this passage?
questions.answer: Those who follow divine law and those who rebel by following their own desires.

questions.question: What does the passage teach about the meaning of the road itself?
questions.answer: It is the path of human existence from its beginning to its ending in the next life.

questions.question: In the comparison, why are worship and fear of Allah important like travel equipment?
questions.answer: Because they help a person carry out life’s journey safely and with protection.

questions.question: What surprising truth does the passage teach about worship?
questions.answer: Even though it looks like a burden, it actually brings remarkable ease.

questions.question: What central belief is spoken during the prayer described here?
questions.answer: The believer declares Allah’s absolute oneness in worship.

questions.question: How does this declaration affect the believer’s view of everyday things?
questions.answer: He sees them as signs leading him to Allah’s mercy and care.

questions.question: What does the believer understand about who gives provision and creates?
questions.answer: He understands that Allah alone does that.

questions.question: What does the passage teach about who controls benefit and harm?
questions.answer: Allah alone controls both.

questions.question: How do Allah’s wisdom and mercy comfort the believer?
questions.answer: They assure him that events are meaningful and that Allah’s kindness is abundant.

questions.question: Once the believer knows all things are under Allah’s command, what response follows?
questions.answer: He turns to Allah for safety and places his trust fully in Him.

questions.question: What effect does this trust have when hardship comes?
questions.answer: It gives the believer firmness and confidence.

questions.question: What is identified as the root of bravery?
questions.answer: Faith and worship.

questions.question: What is identified as the root of cowardice?
questions.answer: Misguidance.

questions.question: How does the passage compare a faithful heart with a merely “enlightened” mind?
questions.answer: A faithful heart remains steady, while a mind without spiritual depth can be full of fear.

questions.question: What does the comet example show about fear?
questions.answer: It shows that people without faith can panic even when they seem intelligent.

questions.question: How does the passage describe human ability compared with human needs?
questions.answer: Human ability is tiny, but human needs and worries are huge.

questions.question: Why is reliance on Allah reasonable for human beings, according to the passage?
questions.answer: Because people are weak and limited, so they need the help of the One who has full power and mercy.

questions.question: What overall conclusion should a reader take from this passage?
questions.answer: Worship and trust in Allah bring strength, courage, peace, and great benefit in the journey of life.
